About Guitar Tone Shootout

What is Guitar Tone Shootout?

Guitar Tone Shootout is a platform that helps guitarists compare different amp tones, pedals, and signal chain configurations side by side. Whether you're trying to decide between different amps, testing out pedal combinations, or just exploring new sounds, GTS makes it easy to hear the differences.

Create shootouts by building signal chains with your favorite gear, process your DI (direct input) guitar recordings through them, and listen to the results in a synchronized side-by-side comparison. You can even generate video comparisons to share with bandmates or on social media.

Key Features

Signal Chain Builder

Build complex signal chains with amps, pedals, and effects. Arrange them in any order and create A/B comparisons to test different configurations.

Neural Amp Modeling

Powered by Neural Amp Modeler (NAM) technology for accurate, high-quality amp simulation. Process your DI tracks through professional-grade amp models.

Tone3000 Integration

Access thousands of professionally captured amp models from the Tone3000 library. Browse by amp type, manufacturer, or use case.

Video Generation

Generate side-by-side comparison videos with synchronized audio playback and waveform visualization. Perfect for sharing on YouTube or Instagram.

How It Works

  1. 1
    Upload Your DI Track

    Record your guitar with a DI box or audio interface and upload it to GTS.

  2. 2
    Build Signal Chains

    Create multiple signal chains with different amps, pedals, and effects to compare.

  3. 3
    Create a Shootout

    Process your DI track through each signal chain to generate comparison audio.

  4. 4
    Listen & Compare

    Listen to the results side by side and decide which tone works best for you.

Technology

GTS is built with modern web technologies and audio processing libraries:

  • Neural Amp Modeler (NAM) - High-quality amp simulation
  • Pedalboard - Audio effects processing
  • FastAPI - High-performance Python backend
  • Astro + HTMX - Fast, modern frontend
  • FFmpeg - Video generation and encoding
